metric.why: Data center demand growth has pushed capacity auctions in constrained regions to record clearing prices, and that cost lands on operators as a non-energy surcharge. Energy-only markets have no equivalent charge and instead expose loads to scarcity pricing during extreme events; the two structures trade predictable overhead against price volatility.
metric.target: Auction results are published directly by the grid operator after each delivery-year auction.
metric.definition: In grid regions with a capacity market, the auction-cleared price paid per megawatt-day for generators to guarantee availability years ahead. Passed through to large loads, it is a fixed overhead on every megawatt-hour a facility consumes, separate from the energy price itself.
